Our story began in 2020, when, after decades of working on the development of the first humanoid robots commercialized worldwide, we founded Keybotic in Barcelona with the goal of developing robotic technology to meet the specific needs of the industrial sector. We encountered dangerous inspections carried out by people because there were no alternatives: a maintenance technician supervising the plant and visually checking the equipment, inspecting confined spaces, or manually reading gauges in areas with toxic or asphyxiating gases.
To address this issue, Keybotic built fully autonomous robot dogs capable of accessing any location a human could reach, including stairs and unstable terrain, for industrial inspections. With this technology, we won first place at the DARPA Robotics Challenge, competing against MIT and the world’s best universities. This victory earned us the highest global recognition in robotics, awarded by the United States government, confirming that our autonomy and fleet coordination capabilities are the most advanced in the world.
The Keyper can access any area, including those dangerous for humans, and autonomously monitor facilities. It detects gas leaks, hot spots, steam leaks, reads instruments, detects intruders, and sends real-time alarms to the control center. Additionally, it generates 3D maps with point clouds to be used by engineering departments. In other words, the Keyper performs fully autonomous maintenance and security routes, inspecting facilities and alerting when there is an issue. This improves personnel safety, increases production uptime, and reduces costs through continuous monitoring and predictive maintenance.

Frederick University (FredU) is an energetic and vibrant private university operating in the Republic of Cyprus. Since its establishment (2007), FredU managed to achieve significant growth, both in terms of student population, faculty members, and academic infrastructure. FredU employs about 250 (fte) faculty, with 4500 students enrolled annually on average and operates from two campuses. FredU is recognized as the University that offers novel and innovative programs of study that address societal needs and, primarily, as the university that exhibits high social sensitivity and responsibility. It offers a broad range of academic programs of study (more than 80) in the areas of Science, Engineering, Business, Arts, Architecture, Media, Humanities, Health, and Education. FredU has also developed the necessary experience and e-learning infrastructure for offering accredited programs of study through Distance Learning and has been awarded with the E-xcellence Associates in Quality label. 
Furthermore, FredU hosts an "UNESCO Chair on Lifelong Learning and Adult Education" since 2020. In the same year, FredU joined the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), becoming one of the founding members of Cyprus' national network. In the latest Times Higher Education Impact Rankings 2023, Frederick University ranked among the top 201-300 Universities, the only University in Cyprus and Greece to achieve this. It has also scored highly for its positive impact and meaningful work on specific SDGs, having ranked 44th globally for Quality Education (SDG4) and 100th for Affordable and Clean Energy (SDG7). As part of its internationalization strategy and further engagement with ERA and EEA, FredU has also joint EU CONEXUS a European University alliance for Smart Urban Coastal Sustainability. Furthermore, FredU has been ranked in the top 200 universities in the world in the QS International Trade Rankings 2023. Being the only Cypriot university to appear in this ranking indicates the strength and dominance of our Maritime Commence & Transport Department in the field.
FredU's academic staff, either organized in multidisciplinary teams or individually, is involved in a wide range of research, educational and cultural activities relevant to their specializations. The research initiatives and activities that are being carried out by its faculty, have been funded predominantly from external sources through competitive national and European programs, including HORIZON Europe/2020, LIFE, ERASMUS+, ESA, FP7 and from Regional Funds (INTERREG). Besides the self-funded creative and other projects, the University staff has implemented or currently running more than 320 RDI and consulting projects, the majority of which coordinated by FredU faculty and researchers. As a consequence, the necessary services have been developed (e.g. Research & Interconnection, Financial, International & Public Relations) that provide the required support for the administrative, legal and financial management of funded projects.

entityDescription: Alpha Impulsion was founded in late 2022 and patented hybrid autophage propulsion, a space launch vehicle architecture proposing to use a solid fuel as the launcher's fuselage and tank for its liquid oxidiser. This disruptive technology removes the need for tanks, which represent half the dry mass, enabling a single-stage-to-orbit trajectory. These simplifications will allow the company to propose the lowest environmental impact ever for a launch service in 2028 and reducing the cost of access to LEO by an order of magnitude. This will allow this European launcher to compete with advantages against the american leader that currently dominates the European smallsat launch market. Alpha Impulsion will provide dedicated launches for smallsats up to 1000kg, evolving towards reutilization capability before 2035 to further improve the launch capacity. In April 2023, the company started developing Ambre, the first autophage rocket, and fired the engine for the first time in January 2024. Most ground tests were done at the present date (10/24), enabling a static fire at the end of the year and an atmospheric flight in early 2025. Going forward from this proof of concept, this technological breakthrough requires a 3-year R&D roadmap on the propulsion system and launcher architecture, which Alpha Impulsion is leading with an increasing number of European partners, being implanted in France and Italy to develop the architecture axis where the required skills are, and working towards a larger scale engine prototype with the University of Glasgow, one of the leading research bodies in autophage propulsion. The technology is also appliable to in-space propulsion for high energy missions (orbit raising, deorbitating, inter-planetary missions) and Alpha Impulsion is starting a line of development for a prototype system with Thales Alenia Space as the prime user.

In April 2023, the company started developing Ambre, the first autophage rocket, and fired the engine for the first time in January 2024. Most ground tests were done at the present date (10/24), enabling a static fire at the end of the year and an atmospheric flight in early 2025. Going forward from this proof of concept, this technological breakthrough requires a 3-year R&D roadmap on the propulsion system and launcher architecture, which Alpha Impulsion is leading with an increasing number of European partners, being implanted in France and Italy to develop the architecture axis where the required skills are, and working towards a larger scale engine prototype with the University of Glasgow, one of the leading research bodies in autophage propulsion. The technology is also appliable to in-space propulsion for high energy missions (orbit raising, deorbitating, inter-planetary missions) and Alpha Impulsion is starting a line of development for a prototype system with Thales Alenia Space as the prime user.
